title: Write a GLSL POP
summary: Official Derivative guide for GLSL POP, GLSL Advanced POP, GLSL Copy POP, and POP buffer access from GLSL TOP/MAT, covering compute thread indexing, selected-class access, output attribute allocation and initialization, array/extra-output helpers, dimensions, groups, and advanced topology outputs.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs GLSL POP compute shader source, selected-class attribute mutation, GLSL Advanced POP topology/output-count work, or GLSL Copy POP source/template access.
For GLSL POP Auto and related thread modes, guard writes with TDIndex and TDNumElements because dispatches can be rounded up to the workgroup size.
For P[id] writes, P must exist in the input or be created, and P must be selected in Output Attributes so the output buffer is allocated.

Output attributes are uninitialized unless Initialize Output Attributes is enabled or the shader writes every value; reading uninitialized values downstream can cause unpredictable behavior and crashes.
Set Output Access to Read-Write when output attributes must be read back or used for atomic operations; otherwise writeonly SSBO access is usually the safer intent.
In Manual number-of-threads mode, TDIndex and TDNumElements are undefined and cause compile errors, so use explicit dispatch coordinates or another thread mode.
Use TDInputNumPoints(), TDInputNumPrims(), TDInputNumVerts(), and TDInputPointIndex() when shader logic needs input counts or index-buffer point lookup.

Use cTDArraySize_Attrib / cTDArraySizePoint_Attrib constants for array attributes, and generated extra-output names such as TDInputNumPoints_OutputName() and oTDPoint_OutputName_AttribName[] for GLSL Advanced POP extra outputs.
For GLSL Copy POP point shaders, use TDCopyIndex(), TDTemplate_Attrib(), and TDUpdatePointGroups() when template-driven copies need per-copy attributes or group preservation.
Use GLSL Advanced POP instead of GLSL POP when the shader must read or write multiple classes, output new element counts, write index buffers, or use per primitive batch dispatch.
Use class-prefixed reads such as TDInPoint_*, TDInPrim_*, and TDInVert_* when reading attributes from a class other than the selected class.
